newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria to privatise national airline Air Algerie.
newsitem.headline: Algeria to privatise national airline Air Algerie.

text.p: Algeria's cabinet has approved a draft law to privatise the national airline Air Algerie and open maritime firms and ports to privatisation, Algeria's state-run television said on Monday.
The law envisages a code of civil aviation "which aims now to permit air transport to open up to private investment and competition," it said, quoting a statement from Sunday's cabinet meeting.
The loss-making Air Algerie has been battered by repetitive pilot strikes over pay. Airline director Faisal Khalil said earlier this year the company could not afford to meet their claims.

The airline operates 41 aircraft, including 10 Boeing 737-200 Advanced and nine 727-200 Advanced models, according to Jane's All the World's Aircraft. It also has two Airbus A310-203 and seven Fokker F27-400M planes.
Air Algerie had a deficit of about 2.0 billion dinars ($37 million) in 1995, mainly because of decreasing demand for flights over the past six years, Khalil said.

Algeria has been hit by violence for the past five years in which about 60,000 people have been killed, including more than 100 foreigners. Foreign embassies have warned their nationals not to travel to the North African country.
The official news agency APS said earlier that ministers had also approved a draft for a maritime code.

"This project aims, in the framework of global action for national development, to open marine transport and port activities to private investment and competition for better fluidity and coordination of trade and marine exchanges," APS quoted the statement as saying.

APS on Monday reported Algeria's director-general of customs, Brahim Chaib Cherif, as telling officials in the western port of Oran that more than 200 containers in the port had been there longer than the regulation turnaround time and were strangling the port.

"All merchandise in the ports having passed the normal time period will, from 1997, automatically be put on sale (by auction) regardless of the nature of the importing company," APS quoted him as saying.
"From now on, ports will serve uniquely as points of transit for merchandise and not a zone of depositing for importers or places where commercial operations are carried out," he said.
